chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Bakr ibn Salih, from Al-Hasan ibn Ali, from Abdullah ibn Ibrahim, from Ali ibn Abu Ali Al-Lahabi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

Rasool-Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Four (qualities), whoever possesses them, and even if he was (immersed) in sins from his head to his toe, Allah would change them to good deeds: Truthfulness, Bashfulness (Hiya), Good Manners, and Gratitude.'
ai.seo_question: What four qualities can turn sins into good deeds according to the Prophet?
ai.summary: In this hadith from al-Kafi, the Prophet (peace be upon him) identifies truthfulness (al-sidq), bashfulness (al-hiya'), good character (husn al-khuluq), and gratitude (al-shukr) as transformative virtues capable of converting a lifetime of sins into good deeds. This reflects the Shia emphasis on these traits as the spiritual antidotes to moral decay, where inner sincerity and outward conduct work in tandem to elevate the believer's status before Allah.
